content.text:
For a **common cold**, medicine won’t cure it, but it can **ease symptoms** while your body recovers. Most colds are viral, so **antibiotics usually don’t help**. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html?utm_source=openai))

**Common options for adults:**

- **Fever, headache, sore throat, body aches:**  
  **Acetaminophen** or **ibuprofen**. Follow the label. Avoid doubling up on acetaminophen—many “multi-symptom” cold medicines already contain it.

- **Stuffy nose/congestion:**  
  **Saline spray/rinse** is safe for most people.  
  A decongestant like **pseudoephedrine** may help, but avoid or ask a clinician first if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, certain prostate issues, glaucoma, are pregnant, or take stimulant/MAOI-type medicines.

- **Cough:**  
  **Honey** can help cough in adults and children over 1 year old. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/acute-bronchitis/about/index.html?utm_source=openai))  
  **Dextromethorphan** may reduce a dry cough; **guaifenesin** may help loosen mucus for a wet cough.

- **Runny nose/sneezing:**  
  Some antihistamines can help, but older ones like diphenhydramine can cause drowsiness.

**Also helpful:** rest, fluids, humidifier/steam, throat lozenges, and warm tea/soup.

**Important safety notes:**
- Don’t give honey to children under **1 year**.
- OTC cough/cold medicines are generally **not recommended for young children**; ask a pediatrician/pharmacist. CDC notes they can cause serious side effects in children. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/acute-bronchitis/about/index.html?utm_source=openai))
- Consider testing for **COVID-19 or flu**, especially if fever/body aches are prominent or you’re high-risk, because antivirals may be an option if started early. ([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html?utm_source=openai))

**Get medical care urgently** if you have shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, blue lips, dehydration, fever that won’t come down, symptoms worsening after improving, or symptoms lasting more than about 10 days.
